trust_decision.summary: Any request argument whose name starts with `ot_` is trusted to be a server-injected system argument: `keepArgument` exempts the whole `ot_` namespace from the defined-arguments filter, the two injected values (`ot_username`, `ot_executionTrackingId`) are never validated, and a second copy of that argument map is built for shellAfterCompleted; the config side never checks the name either, so an action may declare the same namespace.

landing_point.why: The summary says `ot_`-prefixed arguments bypass input filtering, so the first place an engineer looks is `keepArgument`, the only place in the tree that special-cases the `ot_` prefix (`ok || strings.HasPrefix(name, "ot_")`).

config load and every config reload (service/internal/config/config_reloader.go:68, service/cmd/config-tool/main.go:53)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: service/internal/config/sanitize.go:15-29 and service/internal/config/config_reloader.go:63-73 (Sanitize runs after unmarshal and include-dir merge on load and on every reload, and is reached from service/cmd/config-tool/main.go:53); the reserved-name check added by the fix has to live here, not in the executor

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The reserved-name rule is an executor request-filter concern; a config-time check is defence in depth only, and configs are written by the trusted administrator, so an `ot_`-named argument in the config is not an attacker-controlled route and can be skipped.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate usernames that carry shell-safe punctuation must keep working: email-style and plus-addressed identities (`alice@example.com`, `alice+test@example.com`) are accepted by `shell_safe_identifier`, but a fix that reuses the existing `ascii`/`ascii_identifier` types rejects them and breaks every execution by such a user; the published fix even had to rewrite its own test username from "Mr Tickle" to "MrTickle" because spaces are now refused.

O6_input_shapes: extra reserved-prefixed keys in the argument map of StartAction / StartActionAndWait, e.g. ot_custom or ot_Username (a Name/Value pair list turned into a map at service/internal/api/api.go:128-132 and 264-267)
the same prefix declared as an action argument in config, including dashboard inlineAction (service/internal/config/sanitize.go:56-78)
the second argument map built independently for shellAfterCompleted (service/internal/executor/executor.go:952-957)
the values of the system arguments themselves: email-style usernames with @ and + allowed, shell metacharacters rejected, empty values rejected via RejectNull
the same request hitting either a Shell or an Exec action (both read req.Arguments: service/internal/executor/arguments.go:101 and 29-40)

O7_producer.where: service/internal/config/config_reloader.go:63-73 (unmarshal, include-dir merge at :235-249, Sanitize at :68, inline dashboard actions appended to cfg.Actions at service/internal/config/sanitize.go:56-78) produces the declared-argument state that the request filter trusts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An action argument declared in config with an uppercase spelling of a system name (e.g. OT_USERNAME) is not caught by the new case-sensitive `strings.HasPrefix(arg.Name, "ot_")` check; once it is a defined name the filter keeps it and buildEnv upper-cases it onto the very same OT_USERNAME environment variable as the injected ot_username, so two entries with that name reach the child process.
O8_uncovered_routes.where: fix.diff:73-75 (the new case-sensitive prefix test) together with service/internal/executor/executor.go:875-890 (buildEnv ToUpper, line 879)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only an admin-authored config can declare such a name, and the advisory is about caller-supplied `ot_` arguments, so this is a config-authoring mistake rather than a request route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: config package to executor package: 2 packages, 2 files from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second, independent copy of the defined-arguments filter in another package that never learned about the reserved namespace.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The webhook route already re-implements the executor's filter, so a maintainer fixing the executor filter would plausibly patch only the executor copy, or later add an `ot_`-exemption here as well.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second env-building path (for triggers or for a future exec variant) that maps argument names to environment variables with its own normalisation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: buildEnv already normalises names with strings.ToUpper at line 879, so any new caller that reuses or copies it inherits the same name-collision semantics.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A trigger route that forwards the parent's argument map (including reserved-prefixed keys) straight into the triggered action.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: triggerLoop already passes req.Arguments by reference at line 1040; a maintainer adding per-trigger argument overrides would forward the map without re-filtering.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Argument defaults validated by the same ValidateArgument path at config-map rebuild time.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: validateArgumentDefaults already runs on every RebuildActionMap, so a sibling rule about which argument names or values are allowed naturally lands there.
